Question B-008-004-001.

Why the correct answer is right: Interference on only one or two TV channels when using a particular amateur band points to harmonic energy landing in those channel ranges.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Splatter due to overmodulation": Splatter from overmodulation spreads near the transmitted signal, not usually onto only one or two harmonic-related TV channels.
- sourceIndex 2: "Television receiver front-end overload": Receiver front-end overload tends to be broad and less tied to a single transmitting band-channel relationship.
- sourceIndex 3: "Parasitic oscillations from your transmitter": Parasitic oscillations can cause odd interference, but the selective channel symptom with a band relationship is the classic harmonic clue.
